newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Portugal orders 18 A319 jets from Airbus.
newsitem.headline: Air Portugal orders 18 A319 jets from Airbus.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said on Tuesday that TAP-Air Portugal decided to acquire 18 single aisle A319s from Airbus Industrie as part of its medium-range fleet renewal plan.
Five of these aircraft can be converted into A320s.
The company has also taken an option on eight aircraft from Airbus's single aisle family and will lease another four A319s, Airbus said in a statement.

Delivery of the A319s will take place between December 1997 and June 2000. The new aircraft will progressively replace older generation aircraft and make Tap an all Airbus aircraft operator, Airbus said.
It said the A319s won out over planes made by Boeing.
The A319 is the newest and smallest of the Airbus jets. It is a twin-engine, single-aisle short version of A320 and seats 124. Industry sources said an A319 costs about $39 million.

Airbus Industrie (AIN1) is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Aerospatiale and Deutsche Airbus have 38 percent each. British Aerospace Plc has 20 pct and CASA of Spain four percent.
